description: A benchmark-compatible diagnostic adapter for Self-EvolveRec that probes the trained recommender through a stable SASRec interface while restricting analysis to observed public data.
motivation: Preserve useful model diagnostics as architectures evolve, avoid unsupported user or item attributes, and select improvements using the shared macro-average validation HR@10.
implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device) and run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Access the actual trained module through view.model and adapt feature/scoring probes to architecture changes. Preserve item_emb, log2feats, predict_score, user_train, meta_data, and review_data compatibility without fabricating unavailable review content. Loader batches contain (None, sequence, positive, negative), with tensors shaped B x L. Use only interaction histories, titles, descriptions, and timestamps. Treat simulator diversity/conformity traits as unobserved. Generate full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for twenty real training users, five per category. Retain all four datasets and select trials using the pinned validation protocol; never use hidden test data. Update the predictor writer whenever inference architecture changes.
pseudocode:
initialize DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    preserve model training state
    put view.model in evaluation mode
    disable gradients
    for each (_, sequence, positive, negative):
        compute architecture-compatible features and scores
        accumulate valid-position diagnostics from observed data
    generate full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for 5 training users/category
    mark unavailable attributes and traits as unobserved
    restore model training state
    return metrics, metric_definitions
select trials by macro-average validation HR@10 across all four categories

originality.positive: Connects evolving model architectures to a stable, data-constrained diagnostic contract.
originality.negative: Primarily an integration specification; no new diagnostic algorithm is described.

future_potential.positive: Can support consistent diagnosis and model iteration across architectures.
future_potential.negative: Recommendation improvements depend on concrete probes and an effective feedback mechanism, neither specified here.

code_difficulty.positive: Explicit interfaces and batch shapes make the adapter straightforward to implement.
code_difficulty.negative: Architecture compatibility, correct masking, and full-catalog scoring require care. Scores use a 1–10 scale, with higher difficulty meaning harder implementation.
